# The previous attempt to specify resources on a per-task/per-node basis (--ntasks-per-node, --gpus-per-node, --cpus-per-task) failed validation.
# This suggests the system prefers whole-node requests. This version requests 3 exclusive nodes with a total of 12 GPUs (which will be distributed as 4 per node).
# The 'flux mini run' command is then used to specify the precise task, CPU, and GPU layout within the larger allocation.

# The Slurm directive '--ntasks-per-socket=2' is a topology hint that has no direct equivalent in Flux batch options and has been omitted.
# Flux will manage the placement of tasks across sockets.

# The Slurm directive '--mem-per-cpu=0' (requesting all memory on the node) does not have a direct equivalent in Flux and has been omitted.
# The performance implication is that the job may be scheduled on nodes without enough memory, potentially causing it to fail.

export PYTHONHASHSEED=0
module load anaconda
source activate pppl
module load cudatoolkit/8.0
module load cudnn/cuda-8.0/6.0
module load openmpi/cuda-8.0/intel-17.0/2.1.0/64
module load intel/17.0/64/17.0.4.196 intel-mkl/2017.3/4/64

#remove checkpoints for a benchmark run
rm /tigress/$USER/model_checkpoints/*
rm /tigress/$USER/results/*
rm /tigress/$USER/csv_logs/*
rm /tigress/$USER/Graph/*
rm /tigress/$USER/normalization/*

export OMPI_MCA_btl="tcp,self,sm"

# Launch 12 total tasks (4 per node), assigning 4 CPUs and 1 GPU to each task, matching the original Slurm request.
flux mini run -n 12 -N 3 --cpus-per-task=4 --gpus-per-task=1 python mpi_learn.py

export PYTHONHASHSEED=0
module load anaconda

module load intel/17.0/64/17.0.4.196 intel-mkl/2017.3/4/64

rm /tigress/$USER/model_checkpoints/*
